SH3 domains typically recognize proline-rich motifs (PxxP) and can also interact with charged/polar residues at the binding interface.

- N92H (A) introduces a charged histidine
- S83F (B) introduces a bulky aromatic residue
- K85W (F) introduces a large aromatic residue
- I87W (G) introduces a large aromatic residue
- N92S (D) changes asparagine to serine

The N92S mutation in Pbs2 has been identified in studies as increasing the interaction with the SH3 domain. This change from asparagine to serine at position 92 creates a more favorable binding interface for the SH3 domain, enhancing the protein-protein interaction.

[ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
